conclusion: The narrowest theorem upgrade that yields log g(k)=o(k) is a subexponential-in-k bound on the number of solutions of the weighted two-term S-unit equation alpha*X+beta*Y=1, uniform in alpha,beta; a three-line elementary reduction (g(k) <= 2 + E(k), at rank exactly k, no loss) proves sufficiency, and the known extremal lower bound for that equation is exp(Theta(sqrt(k/log k))), which is exp(o(k)) and so does not obstruct the target. Quantitatively the route is today far weaker than Erdos-Turan 1934: Evertse gives g(k) <= 2 + exp(4k+10), base e^4 against base 2.
confidence: High on the reduction and on the implication direction: the proof is four lines, elementary, and its mechanics were re-verified on all seven of the parent's witnesses (identity, S-unit property and injectivity, 165 pair-cases, all pass). High on the two audit corrections, both of which are two-line arguments with an explicit computed witness. Medium on the cited constants (Evertse exp(4s+6), Beukers-Schlickewei 2^(8(r+2)), Erdos-Stewart-Tijdeman exp((4+o(1))sqrt(s/log s))): they come from one web search each and were not read out of the source papers in-session. The comparison 'much weaker than 1934' survives any plausible slip in those constants, but do not quote the exponents as pinned.

notes_for_operator: The deliverable is a sufficiency theorem plus an honest quantitative verdict, not a new bound on g(k). Nobody should read this arm as improving the 1934 constant; it improves the target. If this problem is funded further, the two cheapest next moves are the g(3) <= 7 disposal (finite, kills a whole arm) and the coupled system (the only unread structure). Do not fund additive energy, Freiman or sum-product here: section 4 gives the structural reason each fails, and the energy inequality is measurably dominated by a one-line pigeonhole.
